title: Writing a node that expands into a subgraph
hook: A node can answer with new nodes rather than a result. That is how a graph with no cycles gets loops. Here is one you can write, and how it fails.

verified.claim: A test node with times=3 added nodes 2.0.0.1, 2.0.0.2, 2.0.0.3, and a picture of mean 0.1255 came out at 0.8745.
verified.ref: V1 and V3 test nodes through PromptExecutor on a CPU

verified.claim: A V3 node without enable_expand fails with: Node ExpNoClone is not expandable, but expand included in NodeOutput.
Expanding into an unknown class fails during the run with KeyError 'NoSuchNode'. Validation doesn't see those nodes.
A second queue of the expanded graph ran nothing new.
verified.ref: same run, one executor with the classic cache

verified.claim: Core's Start Loop ran its body 3 times. We ran it in one process with a stub for the server object it reports progress to, and passed validate_prompt's own annotated prompt.
Node ids must be unique across the graph and the same between runs, and GraphBuilder is the recommended way.
With a tensor passed as a value, changing times from 3 to 4 re-ran every inner node: 3 inverts, then 4 more.
verified.ref: test node through PromptExecutor with the classic cache, CPU

unchecked: We didn't run f_core_loop on a real server for this lesson. Our no-server checker validates it but can't run it, because Start Loop calls the server to report progress.
We didn't test raw_link inside expansion, though the docs describe it as the way to keep inner caching.
